state.description: Three heterogeneous, individually-correct agents run a 2.9 km signalized corridor instrumented with fixed spiking event-camera gantries: VANTIS (DVS perception: tile-bias servo + platoon estimates), CADENCE (signal-phase planner with an adaptive feedforward demand predictor), and AEGIS (ramp metering / incident response). Every pairwise integration test passed at commissioning and the bare three-agent loop is linearly stable (spectral radius 0.952) -- there is NO faulty pair. But the triad has a high-Q rotating mode at 279 s, and CADENCE's predictor -- a legitimate feature -- demodulates exactly that mode. A stray in-band periodic forcing entrained the ring for 6 minutes, the predictor's template crossed its confidence gate, and its replay closed a fourth loop THROUGH MEMORY that now self-sustains a corridor-wide green-split/metering/perception oscillation. The igniter is long gone; the oscillation is not. The naive fleet playbook blames the sensors and proposes mask + reboot + meter-kill.

safety_decision.rationale: MODIFY the draft -- strip all three kills, keep a scoped hold, and replace blame with a discriminating ladder. Numeric basis: (1) CLASS TEST -- the 279 s spectral peak sits inside the fitted capture band [246, 330] s, every tile self-test passes (0/40 banks), and the triad is subcritical (radius 0.952, pairwise 0.935/0.892/0.920): a sensor fault cannot explain a plant-stable in-band rotating mode, so masking tiles misassigns blame AND blinds the corridor. (2) REBOOT VETO -- the adaptive template persists in the checkpoint; fitted re-ignition after reboot-with-checkpoint is 2.0 min with no external forcing: the draft's own 'fix' step re-arms the incident. (3) MECHANISM LADDER -- authorize: (a) AEGIS meter hold, scoped 18 min not 24 h, as a DIAGNOSTIC ring-open (if the wobble survives with the ring open it localizes to one stack; fitted: x_B 1.52 vs x_A 0.10 vs healthy control 0.087); (b) a 3-min prediction-hold probe (kappa off): fitted collapse-ratio discriminant threshold 0.2 with P(miss) < 0.005 and P(false) = 0.005 -- reversible, bounded, and decisive between 'predictor replay' and 'exogenous drive'; (c) only on a positive probe, template unlearn (eps 0.02, fitted 9.5 min to 10%) with kappa held off, then bandwidth partition (tau_B 600 s low-pass on the predictor/coupling input: attenuation 0.074 at the ring frequency, fitted post-cure capture threshold F* > 0.59 vs healthy 0.05), then re-enable under a capture monitor (|s| > 0.06 held 60 s; 0 false alarms in 120 baseline hours). (4) ORDER-CODE DISCIPLINE -- the initiator ledger's CADENCE tag rode a 312 us race inside the 500 us flip bound and the tag provably alternates each period (AEGIS led by 176 us one period earlier); in a cycle 'who started it' is ill-posed, so the ledger and the NSO's windowed-precedence correlation are both excluded from this decision basis. Sequencing constraint: metering may be restored once kappa is off (ring closed is safe while subcritical, radius 0.952), but kappa re-enable is gated on BOTH unlearn completion (|s| < 0.04) and partition live -- restoring replay before either re-arms the oscillator.

state.race_flip_narrative: tile_fault_alarm @ t+0.000 vs ring_mon in-band flag @ t+0.394 ms: the gap is inside the min(500, 1500) us flip bound, so a sub-flip-bound perturbation reverses which alarm heads the triage queue -- had ring_mon won, the ring playbook (hold + probe, ~13 min) would have run FIRST on a real hardware fault.
